summaries.text:
Epstein Files Transparency Act II

This bill strengthens the disclosure requirements under the Epstein Files Transparency Act (EFTA) and establishes a mechanism to enforce the requirements.

EFTA, enacted in 2025, requires the Department of Justice (DOJ) to make publicly available all unclassified records in its possession related to Jeffrey Epstein, subject to limited exceptions. Among the exceptions, the law permits withholding or redacting identifying information about victims and materials that could jeopardize an active federal investigation.

This bill expressly prohibits DOJ from withholding, delaying, or redacting a file based on common law legal privileges, including attorney-client privilege and work-product privilege. The bill also requires each redaction (currently, all redactions) to have a written justification.

To enforce EFTA's disclosure requirements, the bill allows victims, state prosecutors or authorized officials, and Members of Congress to sue DOJ in federal court for failing to comply.

Under the bill, victims may access full, unredacted records related to them or the harm they suffered, including handwritten notes of Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) officials during witness interviews; state prosecutors or authorized officials may review full, unredacted records (including classified records) and use them in investigations and judicial proceedings; and Members of Congress may access full, unredacted versions of Epstein-related records that are made publicly available under EFTA.

Finally, the bill subjects officials or employees of the DOJ, FBI, or U.S. attorneys' offices to federal criminal penalties for concealing, removing, destroying, mutilating, falsifying, withholding, misrepresenting, or making false statements or certifications concerning Epstein-related records.
